newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs to remain firm, curve flatter.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs to remain firm, curve flatter.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds will remain firm on Friday, dealers said, with investors continuing to prefer longer maturities over the front end of the yield curve, dealers said.

Few expected any upsets from U.S. producer price and industrial production data due at respectively 1330 GMT and 1415 GMT. "The big number was last week," one trader said, referring to U.S. non-farm payrolls.
U.S. retail sales figures for January, which had been flagged as a possible risk factor in Thursday's session, ended up supporting the market.

Bunds rose against Treasuries on news retail sales rose by 0.6 percent, less than the 0.7 percent that had been forecast by most economists, helping all European core markets hold on to morning gains.
In Belgium, the benchmark 10-year OLO maturing March 2007 was yielding around 5.59 percent at 1600 GMT, down from 5.62 percent in late Wednesday trade.

Dealers said longer maturities, especially the OLO 12 (maturing December 2012) and OLO 23 (maturing March 2015), Belgium's longest maturity, remained the most popular. This was helping all the long-end higher and the curve to flatten.

"If the Bund goes up further we can expect more flattening because the very short end is fixed with the repo and can't go much lower, while the two-to-five year spread is already tight enough," Dirk Laenen at CERA Bank said.
Laenen noted the Belgian yield curve was no different from other core European markets in this respect.

Fears the U.S. Treasury's auction of 30-year bonds, the result of which was to be announced late in the European session, was not going very well did not seem to be pulling the U.S. market lower, he added.
